title: Dynamic Metric Contract Negotiator and Backpressure-Aware Exporter for Inference KPIs
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Tenant-specific inference KPIs (per-model latency, kv-cache hit, token-cost attribution) have heterogeneous schemas and cardinalities. Downstream consumers (Prometheus jobs, billing pipelines) need stable contracts, but edge and dedicated nodes occasionally emit extra labels or large cardinality dimensions causing ingest backpressure and OOMs.

Goal: Implement a contract negotiation layer at the OTLP/prometheus boundary that: 1) advertises a canonical metric contract per tenant and workload, 2) performs runtime schema negotiation and controlled label shedding, and 3) applies backpressure-aware sampling throttles when cardinality or ingestion rates exceed configured SLOs. The negotiator should be pluggable and support both gateway-side and sidecar deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Can accept OTLP metrics with dynamic label sets and produce a stable, documented metric contract for downstream Prometheus scrape/remote_write consumers
Applies label-shedding policies per-tenant without dropping core inference KPIs (latency_p50/p95, tokens_consumed, kv_cache_hit_rate)
When ingestion rate exceeds tenant quota, exporter enters 'graceful-throttle' where low-value high-cardinality series are sampled down and an explanatory metric is emitted
Integration tests validating schema negotiation + backpressure scenario (synthetic high-cardinality generator) pass in CI
End-to-end dashboard in Console showing pre/post-cardinality, dropped_series_by_reason, and latency SLO compliance for a test tenant
tasks: Design contract schema and versioning strategy (contrib: research on label semantics)
Prototype negotiation API (gRPC endpoint) and sidecar adapter for OTLP ingestion
Implement label-shedding policies and policy language (yaml-based ruleset per tenant)
Build sampling engine with burst tokens and decay to avoid feedback loops
Create integration test harness (synthetic metric generator, load scenarios)
Wire Console dashboard and an alerting rule for throttle events
Document migration: how to request new labels and opt-in to extended contracts
progress_updates: 2025-02-14: Kickoff meeting — aligned with PM/Design on user-visible guarantees. Agreed core KPIs that cannot be shed: inference_latency_p50, inference_latency_p95, tokens_generated, kv_cache_hit_rate, request_count.

2025-02-20: Spike completed for negotiation API using proto-based contract descriptor. Prototype pushes a per-tenant contract blob to the gateway and sidecar reads it on startup (PR: github.com/redwood/telemetry/pull/1123).

2025-02-27: Implemented initial label-shedding rules; ran synthetic generator causing high-cardinality churn — negotiated contract held and shed labels as expected. Observed backlog spikes when sampling disabled; sampling engine adjusted to token-bucket with exponential decay.
2025-03-03: Security flagged KMS usage for policy updates in Private deployments — added to security review onboarding.
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Decision: Use OTLP/gRPC as primary ingestion path to support both metrics and correlated traces. Tradeoff: slightly higher CPU vs proto-less gateway but simplifies correlation logic.

Decision: Implement two deployment modes — gateway-side (centralized) for Hosted and sidecar for Dedicated/Private. Tradeoff: more code paths to maintain but needed for isolation and network topologies.
Tradeoff: Label-shedding defaults conservative to avoid losing billing signals; customers can request additional labels via contract/versioning flow (requires release-owner approval).
Rejected: Full dynamic cardinality renormalization in gateway due to complexity — instead we provide signal annotations and sampled series to enable downstream approximate billing when needed.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Incorrect label-shedding could break customer dashboards. Mitigation: emit 'negotiation_change' events and a dry-run mode for the first rollout window.
Risk: Throttle-induced silent loss of chargeable events. Mitigation: maintain a compact sampled-store for billing reconciliation and emit 'throttle_incident' with sample ids.
Risk: Performance overhead on gateway. Mitigation: compile rules to an optimized decision trie and run hot paths in Rust; fallback to a lightweight Go implementation for sidecar.
review_feedback: PM (Lena Zhang): ensure billing edge-cases covered and define a clear opt-in path for customers needing high-cardinality labels.
Design (Ravi Menon): show user flow in Console for 'What changed' after a negotiation update; UX should highlight shed labels and provide contact button.
SRE (Priya Anand): request a canary plan that runs negotiator only for a subset of tenants for 72 hours before global rollout.
